'''AJ Johnson''' (born December 1, 2004) is an American basketball player who last played for the [[Illawarra Hawks]] of the [[NBL (Australia) All-time Records|Australian National Basketball League (NBL)]]. Johnson was ranked as one of the best combo guards in the 2023 class .

== Early life and career ==
Johnson was born in [[Fresno, California]] . He grew up around [[Houston Rockets]] guard [[Jalen Green]] with him considering Green a big-brother .<ref name="Insight">{{Cite web |last=Insight |first=Pro |date=2022-07-04 |title=AJ Johnson Q&A |url=https://www.prospectiveinsight.com/post/aj-johnson |access-date=2024-06-24 |website=Pro Insight |language=en}}</ref>

Johnson in some time in 2020 during the pandemic had a growth spurt going growing 5-6 inches from 5 ft 10 to 6 ft 5 .<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-21 |title=Texas adds No. 25 prospect Johnson to class |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/35075799/texas-adds-no-25-prospect-aj-johnson-recruiting-class |access-date=2024-06-24 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

== High school career ==
Johnson started his high school career at a school in [[Fresno, California]] before spending 2 years at [[Taft High School (Los Angeles, CA)|Taft High School]] where he emerged as one of the biggest risers in part off a growth spurt in the 2023 class being one of the best combo-guards .<ref name="Insight"/> Johnson for his senior year decided to attend  [[Donda Academy]], [[Kanye West]]'s school in [[Simi Valley, California]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Karamanos |first=Alex |date=2022-08-11 |title=BREAKING: 2023 4-Star AJ Johnson will transfer to Donda Academy (CA) |url=https://www.circuitscouting.com/news_article/show/1235505-breaking-2023-4-star-aj-johnson-will-transfer-to-donda-academy-ca- |access-date=2024-06-24 |website=Circuit Scouting |language=en-us}}</ref> Due to Donda Academy's closing  because of multiple controversies surrounding its founder, [[Kanye West]],  Johnson finished his senior year at Southern California Academy .<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-03 |title=Donda players find programs; No. 8 recruit to OTE |url=https://www.espn.com/recruiting/basketball/story/_/id/34941295/top-basketball-recruits-find-schools-donda-academy-closure |access-date=2024-06-24 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>                                                                             
 
Johnson signed with Bill Duffy and WME Basketball .<ref name=":0"/>

=== Recruiting ===
Johnson was seen as one of the best guards and combo guards in the 2023 class . at one point Johnson was ranked as the 9th and 10th best player in the class by [[Rivals.com|Rivals]] , [[ESPN]] , [[247Sports|247]] and On3 . On November 21, 2022, Johnson committed to the [[University of Texas]] choosing [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] over  [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC,]] [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]] and several other high-profile offers such as the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|NBL]] and [[NBA G League Ignite]] .<ref>{{Cite web |last=Conway |first=Tyler |title=5-Star Guard Prospect AJ Johnson Commits to Texas over Louisville, LSU, USC, More |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10056387-5-star-guard-prospect-aj-johnson-commits-to-texas-over-louisville-lsu-usc-more |access-date=2024-06-24 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref>  On April 13, 2023, Johnson announced his decommitment from Texas and announced his plan sign with the [[Illawarra Hawks]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League in Australia]] joining [[LaMelo Ball]] who went from 2nd round pick to potential 1st pick with NBL's Next Stars program .<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2023-04-13 |title=Projected '24 lotto pick opts for NBL over Horns |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/36178252/aj-johnson-decommits-texas-join-australia-nbl |access-date=2024-06-24 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Professional career ==
'''Illawarra Hawks (2023–2024)'''

On April 13, 2023, Johnson signed a contract with the [[Illawarra Hawks]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League in Australia]] joining the NBL's Next Stars program . Johnson joined [[LaMelo Ball]] in 2019 as the other American born prospect to join the Hawks .<ref name=":0" /> Johnson averaged 2.8 points, 1.3 rebounds and 0.7 assists per game in 7.9 minutes a contest playing 25 games during his time with the Hawks .<ref>{{Cite web |title=AJ Johnson International Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/international/players/aj-johnson-1.html |access-date=2024-06-24 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>
